chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umeyra, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Salman saying:
Eat from what the dog catches, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfaly, from al-Sakuny, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said: The Kurdish dogs, when trained, are at the status of the Saluqiyya (Yemeni trained dogs).

key_terms.السَّلُوقِيَّةُ: Saluqiyya, a type of swift, trained hunting dog from Yemen
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: The dog (specifically in the context of hunting)
key_terms.الْكُرْدِيَّةُ: Kurdish (dogs), referring to a specific breed or type of hunting dog
key_terms.عُلِّمَتْ: Trained (feminine plural), referring to dogs trained for hunting

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat from a hunting dog if the dog has already eaten most of the prey?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of consuming game caught by hunting dogs, emphasizing that partial consumption by the dog does not invalidate the meat, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity. It further refines the legal status of different breeds, equating trained Kurdish dogs with the highly regarded Saluqiyya, thereby establishing criteria for valid hunting animals based on training and breed characteristics.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Umeyra, from Aban Bin Taghlub, from Saeed Bin Al Musayyab who said,
‘I heard Salman saying, ‘Eat from what the (hunting) dog catches, even if it has eaten two-thirds of it’.[838] (P.s. – This is not a Hadeeth)
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The dogs of the Kurds, when trained, so these are at the status of the Saluqiyya (Yemeni trained dogs)’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Aban ibn Taghlib from Sa‘id ibn Musayyib who has said the following: “I heard Salman saying, ‘
You can use for food the prey that dogs catch for you even if the dog has eaten two-thirds of it.’”
